summary: All 13 backend tests for the new CrewFit Food Search feature passed (100%). Covered /api/nutrition/food-search (local fallback + chips + short/empty query handling + banana top result), /api/nutrition/food-recent (empty-state + round-trip after POST /api/nutrition/logs), /api/nutrition/food-estimate (Atlas happy path with estimated=true + short-input rejection), and regressions on /api/nutrition/today, /api/nutrition/summary?days=7, the older barcode /api/nutrition/food/search, /api/coach/profile/main (Louis identity), and /api/messages (Louis as partner). Emergent LLM Atlas path returned a valid JSON with source starting with 'atlas' and non-zero macros. No issues found.
critical_code_review_comments: feature_food_search._to_search_result rounds nothing; local kcal/macros come straight from _LOCAL_FOODS (fine). But the search endpoint enforces min_length=1 at the FastAPI layer, so any q='' returns 422 as expected. Confirmed by test.
food_estimate ignores payload._today (it's used only as ai_usage.date). If the client doesn't send it, the record stores empty string – minor telemetry hygiene, not a bug.
seed_data_creation: Test inserts one nutrition_logs row for client@crewfit.com: 'Chicken Breast, Cooked', lunch, 330 kcal, 62/0/7. Persisted in db.nutrition_logs. Not cleaned up (mirrors real user log).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Test suite at /app/backend/tests/test_food_search.py is a good regression harness for future changes to feature_food_search.py. All endpoints prefixed /api/nutrition/food-* are exercised. Auth uses client@crewfit.com / Client123! (JWT from /api/auth/login). The Atlas estimate test relies on Emergent LLM key present in backend/.env – if key is missing it will still pass since the fallback returns 'atlas-local' or 'atlas-placeholder' with source starting with 'atlas'.
